ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $2.69 Ryde voucher to the rider (NS-7 form), record the RD-1 breach on the trip; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a metered RydeTAXI trip, so the distance driven feeds the fare and RD-2's per-km formula governs rather than any fixed-quote analysis [F6][RD-2]. The trace settles that one off-route segment exists and that no traffic incident qualifies under RD-4(a) [F3][F14][RD-4], so the dispute turns only on whether that segment is excused under RD-3 or RD-5.

The chat record for this trip consists of exactly two messages, both sent at 22:43 (rider giving her kerbside position outside Mandarin Gallery; driver giving a 5-minute ETA), and the record is complete and fully timestamped [F7][F8][F9]. Nothing in those words is a route proposal or a route choice, so there is no rider agreement at all — general or named-road — before the segment began at 22:58 [F7][F8][F9][RD-5]. The driver's "Central Expressway was crawling, so I went round it" is a statement written after the trip, not a rider message, and a driver's account of agreement cannot constitute consent [F10][RD-5][G11]. A complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment therefore means the segment counts [RD-5]. The rider also never named a place where the car stopped during this window, so RD-3(a) gives no exemption [F7][F8][RD-3], and F11's band-1 record covering 22:37–22:58 can at most corroborate under RD-4(b), which cannot alone exempt a segment, and its window closes as the deviation begins [F3][F11][RD-4].

Amount: only the unexempted segment's added mileage is refundable [F3][RD-2]. Rate = distance fare ÷ distance km = $18.60 ÷ 13.19 km = $1.41016/km [F4][F6][RD-2]. 1.91 km × $1.41016/km = $2.6934 → $2.69. The remaining 0.60 km between F4's billed 2.51 km and F3's 1.91 km is corridor travel and map-matching noise outside any segment, which RD-2 expressly does not refund [F3][F4][RD-2]. The base $3.90, time $6.72, platform $1.47 and zero waiting fee are not challenged and no unpublished add-on appears, so FARE-1/FARE-2 raise nothing separate [F5][F6][RD-2]. RD-6 requires a prior upheld route dispute in 90 days; the driver has 2 disputes and 0 upheld, so no account flag attaches [F17][RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the rider's two messages and the driver's statement — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F7][F8][F10][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 22:58–23:05 adding 1.91 km. The only chat messages are the two 22:43 pick-up messages, so no rider agreement exists before the segment started and the driver's post-trip statement is not consent [F7][F8][F9][F10][RD-5][G11]; the rider named no place where the car stopped, so RD-3(a) does not exempt the way there [F7][F8][RD-3]; and no incident qualifies under RD-4(a) while band 1 alone cannot exempt under RD-4(b) [F11][F14][RD-4]. Refundable on the segment's added km [RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Reads F10 as showing the driver sought no agreement; that is correct, but it yields no separate or additional remedy beyond the RD-2 refund computed on F3's 1.91 km — a breach with no additional refundable element does not create a further award under RD-2 [F3][F10][RD-2].

Relies on the parties' account histories (rider clean, driver 4.2 years / 1201 trips) to size the refund; profile facts cannot decide any element and the amount is fixed by the segment's extra_km × the trip rate, not by the parties' records [F16][F17][F3][F4][RD-2].
